denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 43775 (laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy) with date of service 2026-06-11. CARC 96: Non-covered charge(s). RARC N130: Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service. Payer remark: Bariatric surgery is a listed plan exclusion.

criteria.text: Bariatric surgery for the treatment of obesity is excluded under this plan regardless of body mass index or comorbid conditions.
Body mass index of 40 or more, or 35 or more with at least one obesity-related comorbidity (type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, or hypertension).
Participation in a physician-supervised weight management program for at least 6 consecutive months within the past 2 years, with monthly visits documenting diet, exercise, and weight.
Psychological evaluation finding no untreated eating disorder, substance use disorder, or psychiatric condition that would impair adherence to the postoperative regimen.
Nutrition evaluation and education on the postoperative diet completed.

Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Polysomnography. Apnea-hypopnea index 28 per hour, oxygen nadir 78 percent. Moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea. CPAP titrated to 11 centimeters of water.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Vitamin D came back 17. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Supervised weight management visit 6 of 6. Weight 253 pounds. Reviewed the food log, 1,500 calorie plan, walking 30 minutes 5 days a week. Drinking more water.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

41 year old woman in bariatric surgery clinic after finishing the supervised program with her primary. Discussed sleeve versus bypass; sleeve preferred given reflux is mild and she wants the simpler operation. Her history otherwise: seasonal allergies. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. BMI 41.7 at 5 foot 5 and 251 pounds. Type 2 diabetes on metformin with an A1c of 7.8, obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, hypertension on two agents.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Pre-bariatric psychological evaluation. No binge eating disorder, no purging, no substance use, depression in remission on sertraline with a PHQ-9 of 6. Understands the lifelong dietary changes. Cleared for surgery.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Registered dietitian evaluation. Reviewed the staged postoperative diet, protein goals of 60 to 80 grams, vitamin and mineral supplementation for life, and fluid separation from meals. Teach-back successful.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Back with the psychology and nutrition evaluations done. Reviewed the operation, the leak risk, and the postoperative diet again. Ready to schedule. Vitals today 125 over 68, pulse 73.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Here with a cough and congestion for 7 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the scheduler.
Blood pressure check. 135 over 81 today, 140 over 74 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Pre-op. Clear liquids for 2 days before, hold the metformin the morning of, CPAP to come with her. Consent signed for laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy.
A1c came back 5.7. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 219, LDL 136, HDL 44, triglycerides 115. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
